prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE finished game environment sprite: a level 1 BASIC MANUFACTURING WORKBENCH, on genuinely transparent background, no text. This is new furniture for the same game as the supplied reference art.
Reference roles: image 1 is GEOMETRY ONLY: its near-orthographic drawing determines camera, rectangular plan, vertical height, contact locations and orientation, not colors or style. Image 2 is the approved STYLE anchor: weighty dark outline, shaped hand-painted light/shadow masses, resolved detail. Do NOT include the man or his pedestal or checkerboard. Image 3 is approved furniture STYLE and lived-in material reference, not an edit target. Image 4 is approved tool-station STYLE reference only: do NOT copy its pedestal, clock, calendar, thermometer, enormous tools, or high backboard.
Subject: a practical compact waist-high salvage workbench for making fishing tackle, rope, everyday tools and containers. One sturdy muted green-grey steel four-legged frame, thick honey-brown repaired wooden plank worktop, small built-in dark iron vise integrated near the operator edge, a shallow lower storage shelf. On one back corner a modest tray with a few wood offcuts and a short loop of cord; most of the worktop stays clear. One replaced pale plank, a small bolted repair plate and wear concentrated beside the vise make it visibly used but functional. This is a modern industrial society still repairing and manufacturing, not ancient fantasy, nuclear wasteland, pristine showroom or glowing sci-fi. Avoid portable hammer/pliers/tools dominating the design; the fixed vise is the identifying feature. No chair, no surrounding items, no ground debris.
Geometry: match image 1 strictly: orthographic ground axes slopes +0.7071 and -0.7071, upright lines vertical, no vanishing point. Logical footprint ONE square tile; table body rectangular 0.95 by 0.70 tile; operator side +Y (down-left facing panel), long axis +X down-right. At 144 px wide tile the worktop rises 42 px above foot contact plane. Four straight legs and lower shelf follow exactly the same axes as tabletop. Keep the entire body and all feet inside frame with a little transparent margin; leg proportions must match guide, not stubby. This is not the lower office desk height. No tall upright back rack, pegboard or lamp at level 1.
Style: strong dark brown-black silhouette outlines, varying interior line weights, restrained clean hand-painted facets, warm wood and desaturated green/grey metal. Light from upper left, clear broad lit/shaded planes, not photorealistic/PBR or uniform micro-scratches. Clear when reduced to roughly 120px overall width. Small objects must stay physically small. Render ONE isolated object at large resolution, 1280 square if possible, fixed camera and generous margins.
CRITICAL output: real alpha transparency, no colored background, no baked floor shadow, NO ground tile, NO floor slab, NO oval or circular display base, NO figure, NO labels, NO grid, NO contact outline drawn on the ground. Only the workbench with its feet. Preserve the distinctive plank layout and leg positions so level 2 and 3 can be made by editing this exact same bench later.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit image 1, the existing manufacturing workbench. Keep its hand-painted style, muted green frame, warm plank wood, pale replacement plank, iron vise, tray, repair plate and lack of a base. Image 2 is the exact GEOMETRY target. Images 3 and 4 are the approved original style anchors (man: line and shading only; office desk: hand-painted furniture only). Output still one transparent isolated object.
ONLY REQUIRED CORRECTION: the current workbench is stretched into a long narrow 2:1 table. Rebuild its drawing to a compact rectangle with horizontal world-plane dimensions 0.95 by 0.70, width/depth ratio 1.36:1, exactly as geometry reference. Short edges must be about 74% as long as the long edges in screen projection. Both ground axes have slopes +0.7071 and -0.7071, with equal projection scale on both axes. Vertical edges remain vertical. This is an orthographic view of a table filling a SINGLE square tile, NOT a 2-tile carpenter bench. Redraw the tabletop and matching lower shelf/leg frame; DO NOT stretch or shear the whole bitmap or its tools. The four legs, shelf and tabletop must form a consistent compact rectangle. Keep the tabletop waist high, vertical rise 42px per144px tile width. Full drawing on 1280-square transparent canvas with all feet visible. The geometry drawing has a pale floor and margins: do NOT copy these.
Keep a flat open working area. Vise mounted on down-left facing operator edge, small offcut tray at back. The tray should be modest, not a quarter of the table. Keep the same three major plank divisions and recognizable pale repaired board, localized worn areas, no additional clutter, no additional furniture. Deep outlines and broad hand-painted light/shadow blocks, upper-left lighting; no PBR, no uniform scratches, no background, grid, labels, ground shadow, floor tile or display plinth.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EXACT EDIT TARGET: the existing level 1 manufacturing workbench. Create its level 2 REINFORCED upgrade on the SAME 1280-square transparent canvas. Images 2 and 3 are ORIGINAL approved style references (man for line/shading quality only, office desk for hand-painted furniture wear). Image 4 is geometry reference only.
Absolute invariants: SAME camera, tabletop four outer corners, leg positions, four floor contact points, silhouette scale, table height, lower shelf height, near pale repaired plank, vise mounting position and wood-tray identity. Do NOT rotate, zoom, move, crop, replace with another table, or change aspect ratio. Preserve every existing foot coordinate. No floor, base or baked shadow. Do not follow the character's pedestal. This is one object, no text.
Upgrade changes ONLY: bolt thicker dark iron corner brackets onto the same four existing legs and add understated cross-braces under the worktop; add an aged dark iron protective rim around the wooden top without extending its outer rectangle; inset a small rectangular worn matte metal working plate into the right-center portion of the same tabletop, leaving the pale repaired plank and large warm wooden areas clearly visible. Strengthen the existing iron vise with a robust but still modest screw housing, in the same place. Tuck one small closed faded canvas parts pouch on the lower shelf, without changing shelf outline. A few localized replaced fasteners and chipped green paint show ongoing repair. Leave the center workspace mostly usable.
The grade must read as the same modest bench made sturdier, not a factory machine. All tiny additions are subordinate to the silhouette and will be viewed at roughly120px overall width beside a90px tall figure. No tall rack, pegboard, portable hammer/pliers, electric cable, glowing lamp or furnace. Keep heavy deep outlines, broad hand-painted light/shadow shapes, upper-left lighting and restrained detail from approved style references. NOT shiny PBR, not photoreal, not noise/scratch covered. Genuine transparent PNG, preserve alpha.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EXACT EDIT TARGET: level 2 reinforced manufacturing workbench. Create its LEVEL 3 PRECISION upgrade. Image 2 (approved man) anchors dark outline and hand-painted shaded volume only. Image 3 (approved office desk) anchors furniture materials. Image 4 (approved tool station) anchors stylized detailing only, DO NOT copy its pedestal/calendar/thermometer. Image 5 is the geometry reference only.
STRICT invariants: Keep SAME 1280-square transparent canvas, identical camera, original same table footprint, top outer corners, tabletop height, lower shelf and four legs/foot contact coordinates. Keep muted green four-legged reinforced frame, metal corner bands and braces, exact pale replaced wooden board, tray of wood offcuts and rope, lower shelf pouch. Do NOT transform the overall table, move or enlarge it, change orientation or crop feet. This is visibly the same table upgraded in place.
Only functional additions for precision grade: evolve the small inset metal working plate at center-right into a slightly larger flat grey-green calibration surface, inset FLUSH into wood (under half of tabletop area), fitted with a compact low mechanical slide fixture, a short guide rail and tiny hand adjustment knob for aligning small parts. Attach a small upright manual screw clamp to the rear edge of that plate, rising no more than about one quarter of the worktop's height above the table. It must look like a manual precision jig, NOT a drill press, electric power tool, big engine or sewing machine. Existing front vise remains in original place and size. Include sparse etched alignment strokes WITHOUT readable numerals or text. Add one shallow fitted small-parts drawer under the back half of tabletop, leaving legs and lower shelf visible and free space between. Keep at least one half of wooden work area clear. No new loose tools or separate apparatus.
Visual read: level 1 = wooden work surface and clamp; level 2 = iron reinforcement; level 3 = precise low mechanical fixture on the same repaired tabletop. Same restrained lived-in state, limited local wear, upper-left light, broad hand-painted planes, warm wooden areas contrasting cool dull metal. Thick clean dark silhouettes and intentionally sparse detail legible at120px overall width. Avoid fine uniform scratches, photoreal/PBR metal and modern glowing electronics.
Output ONE isolated sprite, genuine transparent alpha, no ground/floor/tile, no cast shadow, no grey circular pedestal, no people, no words, no external accessories.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit ONLY the inanimate workshop furniture in image1 into the same workbench BEFORE restoration. Output one isolated game furniture sprite with genuine transparent alpha.
Image1 is the exact object and framing to preserve. Image2 is a hand-painted STYLE reference only: do not draw any person. Image3 provides approved furniture linework and materials. Image4 provides stylized tool-station detail only, without copying its pedestal. Image5 provides geometry only, without its floor, lettering or grid.
Preserve exactly the same canvas framing, camera, object size, original four leg positions, all foot contacts, height and compact single-tile footprint. Keep the grey-green steel frame, wooden tabletop, lower shelf and small tray in their same locations. The table remains fully upright.
Show three clear maintenance needs: the pale replacement plank on the right side has not yet been installed, leaving a large open gap with irregular old wood edges and the support rail visible below; the front bench vise is missing its detachable clamping block and turning handle, with its original fixed housing still mounted; one lower shelf board has a split and a small missing section. The small corner repair plate is not yet fitted, leaving two fastener holes and a split in the wood. Keep the tray almost empty with a short coil of old cord. Add restrained dull rust at metal joints and dusty aged wood, concentrated around these maintenance points. No loose objects on the floor. This should read as the same salvage bench awaiting a few replacement parts, not a collapsed pile.
Match the target's thick dark outline and broad hand-painted planes, warm wood and muted green metal, light from upper left. Preserve vertical uprights and native ground-plane angle. Do not alter stance, rotate, zoom, crop, rescale the object or change perspective. Do not add a person, background, platform, ground shadow, base, floor, text or icons. Real transparency. Keep the entire table and all feet visible.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Make the inanimate workbench in IMAGE 1 MUCH MORE DILAPIDATED. The user wants an unmistakably unusable, severely worn PRE-RESTORATION state, visibly more damaged than the current mild missing-plank version.
Input1 is the EDIT TARGET. Input2 is the SAME bench after restoration, for identity only, do not copy its intact surface. Input3 is original approved linework and hand-painted shading style ONLY, do not draw the person or pedestal. Input4 is approved furniture style/material reference. Input5 is approved device style ONLY, no pedestal or instruments from it.
Keep the same camera, compact single-tile footprint, tabletop frame height, four standing steel legs and foot-contact positions, object size and placement. Keep the complete bench fully within the same square transparent canvas. Preserve the grey-green salvage frame and wooden workbench identity. It stays standing so it can be repaired in place.
Increase damage substantially, with LARGE readable missing shapes instead of more tiny scratches:
- Roughly HALF of the original wooden tabletop is now absent or unusable. Enlarge the existing far/right opening deeply into the center and add an irregular substantial missing section at the front/right corner. Expose the steel perimeter and internal cross-supports through these open spaces. Only a few substantial original timber strips remain along the left/front and far/back edges. Give remaining planks broad lengthwise splits, chipped uneven ends and slight sag; one short fragment hangs down inside the frame. Preserve the steel perimeter corner locations.
- The lower shelf is also roughly HALF missing: a broad central open gap, with short board ends still attached on either side. No continuous intact floor-like shelf. Any loose timber remains caught WITHIN the frame, nothing scattered on the ground outside its footprint.
- The bench vise is conspicuously incomplete: retain its identifiable old bolted mounting plate and ONE short fixed clamping block, with the entire movable clamping assembly and crank absent. The iron fittings have a few broad orange-brown corrosion patches, not photorealistic texture.
- The small upper-left wooden tray has a missing side board and contains only old cord. Remove its tidy usable-box appearance.
- The corner repair plate remains absent. One lower horizontal frame brace is slightly bowed and one joint has a loose fastener; KEEP all four leg bases in their original places and table stance upright.
Materials: duller dusty grey-brown wood with a little original warm color, localized rust and peeling muted-green paint, obvious structural gaps. Preserve restrained hand-painted dark outline and big upper-left-lit shading planes. Large-scale damage must read at about120px total displayed width. No fine all-over scratch noise, PBR or photorealism.
Do not restore any parts. Do not add buildings, people, tools, cobweb scenery, ground debris, floor, display base, baked ground shadow, text or icons. Real alpha transparency including holes THROUGH the tabletop and shelf. No backdrop. No changes to camera, overall scale, orientation or four-foot ground placement.
